No located source specifies this exact five-item exponential-mean SASRec fusion; available sources support individual design choices. The [official SASRec implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/modules.py) specifies zero padding and √d embedding scaling. A reproducible extension should explicitly define r_t = Σⱼ₌₀⁴ λʲmₜ₋ⱼeₜ₋ⱼ / max(Σⱼ₌₀⁴ λʲmₜ₋ⱼ, ε), using only available causal positions, with zero output for empty windows. Specify λ, whether the current item is included, and whether embeddings are raw or scaled. Mask padded outputs after normalization; LayerNorm’s learned bias can otherwise make them nonzero. Matching branch scales or learning a projection is an implementation recommendation, not an established result for this mechanism.

[Highway Networks](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2015/file/215a71a12769b056c3c32e7299f1c5ed-Paper.pdf) motivates negative sigmoid-gate biases, such as −1 or −3. With W=0, b=0 gives gate 0.5, not an inactive branch. [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) establishes zero-initialized residual scaling as an identity-preserving alternative. Algebraically, the proposed outer LayerNorm prevents exact baseline preservation even when the recent-history contribution vanishes: LN(h) generally differs from h. For exact preservation, place the entire correction behind a zero-initialized scalar: z=h+αF(h,r).

Recommended ablations, rather than published findings for this exact mechanism: original SASRec; LN(h) alone; h+cr; LN(h+cr); learned gated fusion. Tune fixed c comparably and include c matching the learned gate’s initial value. Compare learned scalar versus input-dependent gates, raw versus scale-aligned embeddings, and zero versus negative gate initialization. Hold preprocessing, training budget, candidates, and checkpoint selection constant; report four-category macro validation HR@10 and per-category results.
